title: Intro to Redwood - quickstart & deployment options
summary: Discovery focused on Redwood quickstart for Hosted API, questions about time-to-first-token, free credits, and evaluation paths for Dedicated/Private. Customer concerned about latency, cost, and data residency; agreed next steps include sending quickstart guide, pricing worksheet, and scheduling a benchmark deep-dive.

Diego to propose benchmark plan for pilot (by 2026-02-18)
Customer to share traffic profile and success criteria (by 2026-02-16)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Nina Kapoor (ParcelIQ Head of ML), Samir Shah (Eng Manager), Jordan Lee (CTO)

[00:00:00] Maya (AE): All right hi everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick intro, I'm Maya, I'm the AE on this account, and with me is Diego our SE. We thought we'd run through our quickstart experience, how the Hosted API looks, and then talk through your options for Dedicated or Private if that's where you want to go.

[00:00:20] Nina: Thanks, yeah excited to learn more. We moved pretty quickly on the prototypes using some OSS stuff but want a path to production without owning all the infra. Curious about time-to-first-token, how quick the quickstart really is, and what the trial/free credits look like.

[00:00:35] Diego (SE): Sure, great question. For most teams our Hosted API is the fastest path. Typical flow: sign up, get a key, run the quickstart cURL or SDK snippet — you can get your first token in under five minutes. We also provide free credits for evaluation — usually a 30-day credit bundle to exercise latencies and some sample workloads.

[00:00:55] Samir: Under five minutes sounds great, but is that realistic for us? We need to test at our median request sizes and also measure tail latency.

[00:01:05] Diego: Totally. The quickstart gets you started with small samples but for tail and production you can work with us to run a benchmark. For Hosted, you can hit it from your infra and we'll surface per-token latency, token breakdowns in the Console. For Dedicated, you get reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput, which helps with tail.

[00:01:25] Jordan (CTO): What about data residency and security — we can't send certain PII offsite for some flows. Is there a Private option?

[00:01:32] Maya: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem deployments. You can also keep some flows on-hosted while routing sensitive requests to Private or a Dedicated instance. We have KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs.

[00:01:45] Nina: Great. And SSO / SAML? We have strict RBAC needs as well.

[00:01:50] Diego: We support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and also API key rotation policies. For Private we can integrate with your KMS if you want customer-managed keys. Small note — sometimes our docs say KV cash, which is actually KV cache, but we've seen that in the auto-transcripts, sorry.

[00:02:06] Maya: (laughs) that's the transcript gremlin. 

[00:02:10] Samir: Back to quickstart: you mentioned free credits. How big are they? Enough to run a few hours of traffic or a small benchmark?

[00:02:18] Diego: It varies by program but for evals we typically give enough credits to run a small benchmark — say a few thousand requests at typical sample sizes. If you need more for a pilot we can extend it, especially if there's a plan to move to Dedicated after pilot.

[00:02:35] Nina: We're also cost-sensitive. If we start on Hosted and later want Dedicated, what's the migration path? We want to avoid rewriting request logic.

[00:02:42] Maya: Migration is intentionally smooth — same Redwood API across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. You can pin model versions and change routing policies. The biggest lift is around networking and any on-prem packaging for Private.

[00:02:55] Jordan: Any guardrails on model versions, like primary vs fallback? We sometimes need lower-latency / lower-cost fallbacks.

[00:03:02] Diego: Yes, you can set routing policies to prefer lower-cost variants and fall back to higher-performance models on errors. Also features like batching, prefix/KV cache, and quantization profiles are in Redwood Optimize to help trade-off cost vs latency.

[00:03:17] Samir: For latency testing, can we pin the same model in Dedicated? We want to compare Hosted vs Dedicated latencies fairly.

[00:03:24] Diego: Absolutely — we can pin the same model artifact. For a fair benchmark we usually match sequence lengths and batch profiles. We'll provide a benchmark plan: target qps, concurrency, sample prompt set. That way you get apples-to-apples.

[00:03:40] Nina: That sounds good. Quick question on observability — what does the Console show out of the box?

[00:03:46] Maya: Console gives per-route and per-model dashboards, token-level cost/latency breakdown, traces, error rates. It also supports exporting logs for longer retention as an add-on.

[00:03:58] Jordan: Any concerns around vendor lock-in? If we move between providers or self-hosted later, how portable are the prompts and instrumentation?

[00:04:07] Diego: We try to keep the API standard (text generation, chat, embeddings). If you want full portability, we recommend codifying prompts and evals — Redwood supports evals and automated regression alerts to catch changes. Migration of data and model artifacts depends on your workflows, but the API surface is intentionally stable.

[00:04:25] Samir: Are there any limitations on models in Hosted? We rely on some open models that are quantized.

[00:04:32] Diego: Hosted includes a model catalog with curated open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles. If you need a specific variant we can onboard it to Dedicated or Private as part of POC. Some quantized formats may require different runtime paths — we can advise.

[00:04:46] Nina: Ok, let's talk timeline. We're hoping to have a pilot up in two to three weeks. Is that reasonable?

[00:04:52] Maya: For Hosted evaluation yes — you can sign up and be testing in under a day. For a pilot with benchmarks and a Dedicated evaluation, two to three weeks is doable if we get the traffic profile and success criteria this week.

[00:05:05] Diego: We'll need the sample prompts, dataset, and expected qps/latency targets. We'll propose a benchmark matrix — tail p95/p99, median, and token cost per request. Also want to confirm security requirements for Private if that's an option.

[00:05:20] Nina: We'll share that. One more question: for the free credits do we need a card on file?

[00:05:25] Maya: For most self-serve accounts you can claim starter credits without a card. For extended credits or enterprise pilots we usually setup a PO or contract, but we'll make sure you can start quickly.

[00:05:35] Jordan: Any notes about rate limits we should expect on Hosted? We have bursty traffic patterns.

[00:05:40] Diego: Hosted has tiered rate limits; for evaluation you get basic quotas. If you need higher burst we can whitelist for the pilot or suggest Dedicated for predictable throughput. We'll include guidelines in the quickstart doc.

[00:05:52] Samir: Great. Can you also share a simple SDK snippet showing authentication, a sample generation call, and streaming? We want to show the team how quick it is.

[00:06:00] Maya: Absolutely — we'll include a Node and Python example, plus a curl snippet with streaming and how to measure time-to-first-token.

[00:06:08] Diego: One minor tip — time-to-first-token depends on model size and sequence length; for smaller context windows we often see single-digit milliseconds median in Dedicated infra but Hosted will vary by region and model. We'll capture expected ranges in the bench plan.

[00:06:23] Nina: Perfect. This is helpful. Any compliance docs (SOC2, ISO) you can share now?

[00:06:28] Maya: Yes I'll send our compliance pack and the security questionnaire answers after this call.

[00:06:33] Jordan: Alright, let's recap next steps.

[00:06:36] Maya: Recap: we'll send quickstart + free credits instructions, SDK snippets, compliance docs, and Diego will draft a benchmark plan. Nina will share traffic and success criteria. We'll aim to schedule the SE deep dive next week. Anything to add?

[00:06:52] Nina: Sounds right. I'll get the traffic profile and prompts into a Google doc and send it over.

[00:06:58] Samir: Thanks, appreciate the quick overview.

[00:07:01] Diego: Thanks everyone — one last note, if you want we can also run a short smoke benchmark from your region to illustrate latencies vs cost.

[00:07:09] Jordan: That'd be great. Thanks all.

[00:07:12] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up with notes.

End of call.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional misspellings/auto-transcript artifacts. References: quickstart guide link (shared in follow-up), pricing worksheet, compliance pack (SOC2/ISO).
